senses.definition: (archaic or dialectal) simple past of sing
examples:
1862, Mary Elizabeth Braddon, Lady Audley's Secret
It was one of those serene and lovely mornings that sometimes succeed a storm. The birds sung loud and cheerily […]
The August Prince's First Officer […] sung a song; although it was unaccompanied by dancing it was very delightful.

quotes.text: And they sung as it were a new song before the throne, and before the four beasts, and the elders, and no man could learn that song but the hundred and forty and four thousand, which were redeemed from the earth.

quotes.text: Lulled by the Syren-song that my own heart sung to me, with eyes shut to all sight, and ears closed to all sound of danger, I drifted nearer and nearer to the fatal rocks.
